jpm.reviewed_text:
| |  | North America Equity Research  
---|---  
  
# Celestica

## 3Q26 Review: Revenue Outlook Sets a Solid Start for 2027, While Positive
FCF in 2028 Should Ease Concerns; Reit OW

  
---  
  
By Joseph Cardoso
AC,
Manmohanpreet
Singh,
Marc
Vitenzon

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
CLS, CLS US  
Price (27 Oct 26):$276.54  
Price Target (Dec-27):$485.00  
  
Celestica’s 3Q26 earnings print and Investor & Analyst Day continued to
highlight a robust demand environment that helped the company deliver a strong
2027 revenue guide (+90% y/y), which is already well ahead of sell-side
consensus, and screens even more bullish given management’s typical
conservatism on guidance. The strong demand environment also carried into
initial color on 2028, with management indicating revenue meaningfully higher
than 2027 based on design wins already in hand. Importantly, we believe
management has several levers to deliver upside to guidance: (1) Better supply
availability (e.g., silicon); (2) Winning additional custom ASIC programs,
with hyperscalers and frontier AI labs exploring a broad range of
architectures (custom ASIC TAM estimated to expand 7x to $434 bn in 2030); and
(3) Continued market share gains in successive generations of networking
switches, potentially helped by its early leadership in scale-up Ethernet and
CPO-based switching (expected to ramp in 2H27), against an expanding TAM (DC
Ethernet estimated to expand at 40%+ CAGR to $173 bn by 2030). Beyond the top
line, we also see upside to the operating margin guide of 9.0% in 2027 (+60
bps y/y) and the implied gross margin guide of ~11% driven by opex leverage on
stronger revenue growth as well as better-than-expected revenue mix,
respectively. Although revenue and margin trends tracked largely in line with
our expectations and well ahead of consensus (see preview
here), FCF guidance was more limited; however, management pointed
to a net cash outflow in 2027 (JPMe of -$3 bn), with the actual magnitude
being contingent on the revenue growth delivered through the year. Notably,
management framed 2027 as an investment year and expressed confidence in
turning FCF positive in 2028, which should help ease investor concerns about
additional capital raises. To that end, we are updating our model to reflect
the latest guidance, which lifts our out-year earnings forecasts by a mid- to
high-single-digit percentage on average and continue to rate Celestica shares
Overweight, as we see the company as well positioned to benefit from an
expanding compute TAM, supported by a broadening set of custom ASIC programs,
as well as a growing networking TAM, where the scale-out opportunity is being
reinforced by a blossoming scale-up opportunity.

  * 3Q26 Results: EPS beat driven by revenues and operating margins tracking ahead of consensus expectations. Revenues tracked to $5.83 bn (vs. JPMe of $5.71 bn, consensus of $5.46 mn and guidance in the range of $5.25 - $5.55 bn), driven by CCS revenue of $4.87 bn (vs. JPMe of $4.80 bn and consensus of $4.4 bn) or +102% y/y, driven by Networking growth of +68% y/y and Compute & Storage growth of +242% y/y, while ATS tracked to $957 mn (vs. JPMe of $906 mn and consensus of $896 mn). Gross margins tracked to 11.2% (vs. JPMe of 11.4% and consensus of 11.5%), due to mix shift towards Compute & Storage, which in combination with disciplined opex (2.7% of sales vs. JPMe of 2.9% and consensus of 3.1%), translated into operating margins of 8.5% (vs. JPMe of 8.5% and consensus of 8.4%) and EPS of $3.30 (vs. JPMe of $3.05, consensus of $2.96, and guidance of $2.88 - $3.08).
  * 4Q26 Guide: EPS tracked modestly softer than consensus as dilution from recent equity raise more than offset the in-line revenues and modestly better margins. Revenue is guided in the range of $6.275 - $6.575 bn, or $6.425 bn at the midpoint (vs. JPMe of $6.89 bn and consensus of $6.40 bn heading into the print), representing growth of over 75% y/y at the midpoint. Relative to segments, ATS revenues are guided to low-20% y/y, Networking to ~65% y/y, and Compute & Storage to ~160% y/y. Operating margins are guided to track to 8.7%, modestly ahead of both JPMe and consensus of 8.6%. Finally, EPS is guided to track to $3.37 - $3.57, or $3.47 at the midpoint, vs. JPMe of $3.60 and consensus of $3.49). Importantly, FCF for the full year 2026 is lowered to $460 mn (vs. prior guide of $600 mn and JPMe of $466 mn), due to targeted working capital investments to support the accelerating growth in 2027.
  * 2027 Guide: Revenues, margins and EPS tracked ahead of JPMe and consensus expectations. Celestica guided 2027 revenue to $40.0 bn (vs. JPMe of $38.9 bn and consensus of $35.9 bn), representing growth of +90% y/y, a step up from the +69% implied by the updated 2026 outlook, with CCS guided to ~110% y/y and ATS to ~10% y/y. Operating margins are guided to a record 9.0% (vs. JPMe of 8.8% and consensus of 8.7%), translating into EPS guidance of $21.50 (vs. JPMe of $21.30 and consensus of $19.84). Capex is guided to $1.5 - $2.0 bn (vs. JPMe of $1.8 bn heading into print), which along with working capital requirements to support robust growth is driving FCF guidance to a net use of funds.
  * Continued HPS investments to keep Celestica positioned well for the rapidly expanding custom ASIC opportunity. Celestica highlighted its role supporting leading custom ASIC deployments, including Google TPU programs and OpenAI’s Jalapeno architecture, underscoring its differentiated position in designing, industrializing and manufacturing complex system-level AI architectures. Management also emphasized continued investment in HPS, including $300 mn+ R&D spend in 2027, as its design capabilities expand beyond traditional networking switch platforms into custom ASIC compute and rack-scale systems. Importantly, the custom ASIC TAM is expected to grow from ~$61 bn in 2026 to ~$434 bn by 2030, or representing a ~64% CAGR vs. ~28% for merchant GPUs.
  * Highlighted a robust TAM and market share across Data Center Ethernet market. Celestica highlighted that Data Center Ethernet TAM is expected to grow from ~$44 bn in 2026 to ~$173 bn by 2030 (implying 40%+ CAGR), driven by 800G+ expanding more than 7x over the same period. Within this, Scale-up Ethernet is expected to ramp from ~$1 bn in 2026 to ~$55 bn by 2030, representing ~32% of the total Data Center Ethernet switching market and ~40% of back-end Ethernet switching. Celestica’s current position appears strong, with the company citing 31% revenue share in 800G+ Ethernet switching and 44% share of 800G+ port shipments.

redburn.subject: Celestica (Buy): Strong revenues, reassuring free cash flow
redburn.reviewed_text:
# Celestica (Buy)

### Strong revenues, reassuring free cash flow

Celestica’s revenue trajectory continues to be appealing, with FY27 growth guided to +90% YoY. Investor appetite for the stock, however, has been held back by concerns over the free cash flow implications of this growth. We take a sanguine view: management expects to return to positive free cash flow in FY28 and our own stress test validates this in all but the most severe circumstances. We raise our FY27 revenue outlook by 9% with improved operating leverage delivering a 20% FY27 EPS upgrade. This implies Celestica trades at an 11x non-GAAP P/E. We increase our DCF-derived price target to $477 (from $450) and maintain our Buy recommendation.**Read Full Report **Mike Harrison +44 20 7000 2079 | Mike.Harrison@rothschildandco.com Ayana de Zoysa +44 20 7000 2036 | Ayana.deZ

---|---  
  
# Seagate

## F1Q27 Review: Pricing-Led Beat & Raise May Fall Shy of a High Bar; However,
EB Acceleration and HAMR Ramp Lie Ahead

  
---  
  
By Joseph Cardoso
AC,
Manmohanpreet
Singh,
Marc
Vitenzon

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
STX, STX US  
Price (27 Oct 26):$667.85  
Price Target (Dec-27):$1,050.00  
  
Seagate delivered F1Q27 revenue, margins, and earnings ahead of consensus,
driven by a substantially stronger pricing environment as ASP/TB growth
accelerated to +32% y/y (vs. +11% in F4Q26 and -8% a year ago). However, the
F1Q27 results may nonetheless fall short of elevated buy-side expectations,
particularly as exabyte growth (+21%) and cost/TB reductions (-7%) tracked
more subdued. That said, as it relates to exabyte growth, management
highlighted that staged Mozaic 4 inventory should drive a meaningful step-up
in exabyte growth in F2Q27, while underscoring that there are no underlying
supply or product transition issues. Meanwhile, the more tempered cost/TB
reductions were driven by higher external component costs, where management
emphasized its ability to pass through pricing to more than offset the
pressure, while also noting that internal cost improvements remain on track.
Importantly, the F2Q27 outlook points to an acceleration in revenue growth,
led by strong exabyte and pricing growth, as well as continued margin
expansion, which management expects to sustain through the remainder of FY27.
This is supported by a favorable pricing environment and the expansion of
Mozaic 4 beyond the two leading CSPs, with additional global CSP and
enterprise OEM qualifications expected over the next few months. Together,
these dynamics underpin the reiterated target for HAMR to represent ~50% of
nearline EB shipments exiting F2Q27 (Mozaic 4 accounting for 50% of HAMR
shipments) and ~70% exiting F4Q27. With areal-density gains underpinning
supply growth, management underscored its confidence in sustaining mid-20%
long-term EB growth with relatively flat unit production and capex maintained
at 4-6% of revenue. Despite this planned supply growth, management indicated
that cloud and enterprise OEM demand continues to outpace supply, further
widening the supply-demand gap, as inference and agentic workloads increase
data retention and installed AI infrastructure continues to generate new data
beyond the initial buildout. This strength is reflected in longer customer
commitments, with the vast majority of nearline EB supply allocated through
CY28, some cloud agreements extending through CY30, and planning discussions
reaching even further. To that end, we continue to believe the print
reinforces a constructive supply-demand backdrop for Seagate and the broader
HDD industry, with continued pricing strength and an anticipated acceleration
in EB shipments supporting further margin expansion and earnings growth. We
raise our FY27/FY28 EPS estimates, reflecting stronger ASP/TB assumptions, and
reiterate our Dec-27 price target of $1,050.

  * F1Q27 (Sep-end) Results: Earnings beat driven by margins tracking ahead of forecasts. Revenues tracked to $4,233 mn (vs. JPMe of $4,249 mn and consensus of $4,113 mn), driven by robust data center demand driving data center revenue of $3,449 mn (+63% y/y). Gross margins tracked to 57.8% (vs. JPMe of 57.4% and consensus of 57.4%), or +500 bps q/q, reflecting the favorable pricing environment driven by a significant gap relative to demand and supply. Opex discipline (7.1% of sales vs. JPMe of 7.1%) helped further in driving record operating margins of 50.7% (vs. JPMe of 50.3% and consensus of 50.4%), translating into an EPS beat, with EPS tracking at $7.68 (vs. JPMe of $7.58 and consensus of $7.39). 
  * F2Q27 (Dec-end) Guide: Better-than-expected guide across revenue, margins and EPS. Revenue guidance tracked to $4,700-$4,900 mn (vs. JPMe of $4,621 mn and consensus of $4,508 mn heading into the print), with EPS guidance of $9.00-$9.40 (vs. JPMe of $8.68 and consensus of $8.43). Operating margin is guided to mid-50% (vs. JPMe of 52.9% and consensus of 53%), including opex of ~$300 mn (vs. JPMe of $301 mn); and an implied gross margin of ~60% (vs. JPMe of 59.5% and consensus of 59.0%) with pricing growth acceleration to at least 33% y/y (vs. JPMe of +26% y/y heading into the print).

ubs.subject: UBS: Seagate Technology Holdings PLC "Another Solid Quarter, But The Cyclical..."
ubs.reviewed_text:
Amid some noise on ASP and volumes, our thesis here remains the same as the
multiple should continue to contract.  
|  |  | Global Research   
28 October 2026  
---|---|---  
| Seagate Technology Holdings PLC| ●| (STX.O) Neutral|  
---|---|---|---  
| Another Solid Quarter, But The Cyclical Debate Remains The Same;
Neutral  
---  
| Amid some noise on ASP and volumes, our thesis here remains the same as the
multiple should continue to contract.  
  
| | Read Report   > |   
---|---  
| **STX PE and EPS LT trajectory**  
---  

  
Source: Company reports, UBS, FactSet.  
| Summary Thoughts STX posted another solid quarter despite near-term noise
surrounding Exabyte (EB) shipments as pricing continues to strengthen - a
trend that should persist as demand still significantly exceeds supply. That
said, we received many inbounds tonight latching onto a perceived deceleration
in EB supply as a bullish indicator - an argument that we don’t think really
holds water. We model total industry EB supply to accelerate especially as WDC
completes its HAMR transition. Our view here continues to be that Street
numbers are even now still too low, but we don’t think the market should be
paying a higher multiple for HDD stocks than DRAM stocks and that’s not the
case today - ergo, we see multiples here compressing further. Net, we lower
our estimates slightly - with CY28E revs/EPS from $36.2B/$111.63 to
$35.6B/$107.41 - while we maintain our 7x multiple. As such, we trim our PT
from $780 to $750.Analysis/Key Highlights

  * Results: STX reported Sept Q (FQ1) slightly above the top of guidance range, with revenue of $4.23B in-line with UBSe. Bit shipments of 220EB were ~10% below UBSe while ASP per TB was $18.52, up 16% Q/Q. Owing to higher pricing, GM and OpM were both ~30bps ahead of our expectations, and non-GAAP EPS of $7.68 was ~2%/~9% ahead of UBSe/Street $7.56/$7.07. 
  * Guidance: Management guided Dec Q (FQ2) revenue of $4.8B ± $100MM - slightly below UBSe of ~$5.0B but ~6% ahead of Street - as STX benefits from increasing mix of higher capacity drives coupled with stronger pricing. Operating margin was guided to "towards mid-50%" and opex to ~$300MM, which to us implies gross margin around ~61%, in-line with UBSe and 300bps ahead of Street estimates. Non-GAAP EPS guidance of $9.20 ± $0.20 is above the Street but slightly below UBSe. Looking at the opex guidance and backing into OpM that is assumed at the midpoint of revenue and EPS guidance, this implies OpM more in the 54-55% range versus the stated "toward the mid-50%". Ergo, we conclude that the guidance is overall conservative, though we do acknowledge the pressure on cost downs in the near term due to inflationary external component costs. 
  * Pricing/Costdowns: Management suggested that strong customer demand is underpinning today's pricing environment, with ASPs stepping up as contracts roll over and increasing at a rate higher than cost inflation - consistent with its pricing strategy over the past three years. This underpins our assumption of +HSD-LDD% Q/Q ASP per TB increases throughout FY27. At the same time, technology improvements and manufacturing efficiencies are driving lower cost/TB, although external component costs are a headwind in the near term. 
  * Gross Margin: That said, while pricing is expected to push margins higher, external component costs are proving to be a headwind in the near term. Additionally, while HAMR is margin accretive on a run-rate basis, management expects a typical 1-2 quarter lag before getting back to normal yields following the product transition. We model gross margins exiting CY27E at 75.3% and peaking in mid-CY28E at 77.8% before modeling our projected downcycle. 
  * EB Growth: Despite flat EB shipments in Sept Q driven by product transitions, management guided to a meaningful step-up in shipments in Dec Q. STX reiterated its mid-20% Y/Y EB CAGR as demand expands beyond Enterprise and OEM customers. While volumes are generally set for the next 4-5 quarters given the company's BTO construct, STX does not see any demand destruction beyond this timeframe despite the higher pricing environment.
  * Customer Contracts: The vast majority of Data Center nearline supply is allocated through CY28, with some cloud supply agreements extending through CY30. STX mentioned that pricing discussions generally happen 2-3 quarters ahead, indicating that it has visibility into pricing on shipments throughout CY27. Compared to WDC, we continue to prefer STX's approach of limiting contracts to the drives' production lead time of approximately a year, with only non-binding discussions further out than that.
  * HAMR: The ramp of HAMR remains on track as Mozaic 3 products are now qualified across all major hyperscalers, while Mozaic 4 drives (11 4TB platters) are currently ramping with the first two major CSPs; additional CSP and Enterprise/OEM qualifications are expected to complete in the coming months. Overall, STX ended FY26 with HAMR-based products accounting for 40% of nearline EB shipment run-rate, and management remains confident in exiting CY26 with Mozaic 4 at 50% of HAMR EB shipments. Looking ahead, STX expects Mozaic 5 qualifications in late CY27. 
  * Toshiba: When queried on recent headlines related to Toshiba adding significant capacity and aggressive share gain targets, the company responded with similar commentary to what WDC said. That is to say that STX/WDC are such larger scale than Toshiba that if they continue to grow EB at this pace, it would require an unrealistic amount of capacity to be added by Toshiba to meet its share gain aspirations. That is all fine and well, but as we said in our WDC note (here), we have indicated for some time now that several large hyperscalers have been pushing to backstop significant capacity addition by Toshiba in an effort to break the current quasi-duopoly. 
  * TDK: When queried on recent headlines related to bidding for TDK (here), the company had no comment other than to reiterate that HAMR cycle times are longer so in order to maintain flat HDD unit production, it needs to complement the HAMR ramp with more heads and media - some of which it is buying externally. We have always found it odd that if Toshiba's capacity aspirations should be so heavily discounted, why would STX be interested in taking control of TDK (a major head supplier to Toshiba).

Read-Across Commentary surrounding the strong demand environment reads
positively for Seagate's direct peer, WDC, as well as head supplier TDK. More
broadly, this underscores the continued robust demand at hyperscalers, bullish
for most names within our coverage which are levered to the AI data center
theme.Valuation: PT $750 (from $780) We trim our PT from $780 to $750, based
on CY28E EPS of $107.41 (from $111.63) applied to a target multiple of ~7x
(unchanged).  
---

This is Sales Commentary Only, Not Research.****** ** You can find below some
bogeys and important set-ups from Fenske and team…** ****GOOGL SETUP &
EXPECTATIONS - Reports Wed, 10-/28, post-close**

  * **Justin Post’s GOOGL preview**

  * **OVERALL** : Stock has fallen a bit out of favor in the past few months (Deep Mind departures, and other frontier models, including META maintaining more observable ‘momentum’, and in general rise of META as a stock/and MUSE success). The concern that Search could modestly miss has also weighted a bit on the stock. GOOGL expected to continue to spend aggressively on AI/Capex (Head of GOOGL AI Infra on Sequoia podcast continue to highlight demand outstripping supply, among other things)
  * **SEARCH** : Healthy ad checks intra-qtr in Justin’s calls, Justin is modeling 14% Y/Y.  Our conversations suggest buyside is fairly well braced for a possible ‘miss’ vs consensus this qtr (which is 14.6% now), given what 3rd party data is predicting (we’re told). Creates interesting setup for possible ‘better than buyside’ Search print, Justin notes. Justin thinks it would be helpful / upside if we heard “Greater transparency on AI metrics, including AI search query mix, conversion rates for AI versus traditional queries, and AI workload share in Cloud,
  * **CLOUD / TPU.** Buyside modeling over 100% Y/Y growth in our bogey poll, Justin’s modeling 93% Y/Y. Looking out to ’27-’28 - feels like a fairly wide range of EPS outcomes we’re hearing, or maybe better put, a disconnect between buyside (higher) and sellside (not as high) on TPU contribution math/ramp…In his preview Justin Post does point to 2027 TPU sales as the ‘upside’ case not yet fully appreciated
  * **GOOGL - BUYSIDE EXPECTATIONS WE PICKED UP**
    * Q3 Total Rev Growth – **27%**(Street 25%)
    * Q3 Google Search Rev Growth – **15%** (Street 14.6%)
    * Q3 YouTube Rev Growth – **12.1%**(Street 11.3%)
    * Q3 Cloud Rev Growth – **101.1%** (Street 91%)
    * 2027 GAAP EPS – **$18.71**(Street $15.47)

 **MSFT SETUP & EXPECTATIONS – Reports Wed, 10/28, post-close**

  * **OVERALL - LAST QUARTER FELT LIKE A BIG INFLECTION:** MSFT shares are up ~34% since reporting 4Q26 results, following 43% Azure growth. Our CIO survey highlights MSFT’s breadth across the enterprise AI stack, from infrastructure and cloud to security and applications. MSFT leads cloud-infrastructure AI consideration at 88.4%, while 76.7% of respondents use or plan to use Copilot in production. Tal views Azure growth as the key metric into the print, but also flags Copilot adoption and monetization as an emerging growth lever beyond Azure, with the redesign supporting MSFT’s push to make Copilot the operating system for enterprise AI.
    * Last qtr was a huge beat/raise on Azure relative to expectations. Biggest beat in over a year. 
    * They 50% Q/Q increase in Copilot subs was also a big positive surprise data point. 
    * Bulls say….MSFT 365 monetization remains underappreciated; shift to broader consumption based pricing in June, usage has ramped; more ‘subs’ attaching advanced AI usage could drive higher aggregate ARPU
  * **KEY METRICS / 1Q27 EXPECTATIONS: AZURE GROWTH, CAPEX AND M365 CLOUD GROWTH.** Tal models Azure growth of 44.8% YoY cc under the new reporting definition (we heard bogey of 46%, see below), with revenue of ~$32.3bn. He remains constructive on capacity expansion, with MSFT adding ~1GW per quarter to support conversion of its backlog into revenue. On capex (incl. finance leases), expects $50.8bn, up 45.6% YoY, versus Street at $51.8bn. For M365 Cloud, Tal/Street model growth of 15.9%/16.0% YoY. Beyond Azure and M365 cloud growth, watching for continued Copilot paid-seat momentum after seats reached 30mn in 4Q26, up from 20mn in 3Q26.
  * **GUIDANCE / OUTLOOK:** Tal expects modest Azure acceleration into 2Q27, modeling 45.1% YoY cc growth. Compute capacity delivery and efficiency gains remain central to the outlook: GPU deployment times in MSFT’s largest regions fell nearly 50% over the past year, while hardware and software optimization increased Copilot workload throughput 4x. Focus will be on whether these gains continue translating into incremental Azure revenue. For FY27, he models capex (incl. finance leases) of $220.7bn, up 51.9% YoY, slightly above Street at $218.6bn, as MSFT continues its extensive capacity buildout.
  * **MSFT BUYSIDE EXPECTATIONS WE PICKED UP**
    * Q1 Azure growth constant currency – **46%**(Street 44%)
    * Q1 M365 Cloud Rev growth – **16.7%**(Street 16.7%)
    * Q2 guide on Azure cc growth – **46.1%**(Street 40.6%)
    * FY27 Capex (including leases) – **$230B**(Street $218.8B)
    * FY28 Capex (including leases) – **$290B**(Street $247B)
    * FY27 GAAP EPS – **$20.24**(Street $19.72)
    * FY28 GAAP EPS – **$24.27**(Street $23.47)

** ****NOW SETUP & EXPECTATIONS – Reports Wed, 10/28, post-close**

  0. Tal’s NOW Q3 preview
  1. **OVERALL:** Tal expects NOW’s 3Q26 results at or above expectations and sees AI and security adding to an already strong growth business with revenue of $16.2bn for FY26, up 22.1% YoY, and $19.2bn for FY27, up 18.5%. Supporting this outlook, our proprietary CIO survey highlights demand for both the core business and AI opportunity: 42% of respondents rank ITSM/ITOM among their top five spending priorities, while 54.5% are likely or very likely to use NOW for back-office AI. 
     1. Tal reiterates Buy and raises the PO to $180 from $150, based on 27x FY27E EV/FCF.
  2. **KEY METRIC: cRPO AND UNDERLYING ORGANIC GROWTH. **Tal thinks the key debate is whether NOW can sustain growth and covert AI interest into incremental customer spending. He remains constructive given continued demand for core ITSM/ITOM and the rollout of broader AI offerings and expects 20.0% YoY cc cRPO growth in 3Q26 and subscription revenue of ~$4.0bn, up 20.6% YoY (+18.5% organically) vs Street at 20.8%. Healthy upside in cRPO would reinforce confidence in underlying demand. On profitability, Tal/Street model operating margins of 31.1%/31.2%.
  3. **AI AND SECURITY ADD TO THE GROWTH STORY** : NOW’s ownership of workflow context and historical data supports lower-cost AI implementation versus third-party alternatives. Control Tower also positions NOW to help customers govern AI across models and providers, while consumption offers another path to monetization. AI ACV exceeded $1bn in 2Q26, with management targeting $1.5bn by year-end. Lastly, security presents an incremental growth opportunity, with Armis and Veza broadening the offering and supporting cross-selling into the core as enterprises look to onboard AI in a governed and safe way. Security & Risk already exceeds $1bn in ACV and featured in 16 of NOW’s top 20 deals in 2Q26, with 24 deals over $1mn. Continued traction would support growth beyond ITSM.
  4. **NOW BUYSIDE EXPECTATIONS WE PICKED UP**

  * Q3 cc cRPO growth –**20.9%**(Street 19.7%)
  * Q4 cc cRPO growth guide –**20.4%**(Street 19.8%)
  * FY26 Sub Revs – **$16.01B**(Street $15.76B)

** ****ORACLE ANALYST DAY SETUP & EXPECTATIONS – Wed, 10/28**

  0. Tal’s ORCL Investor Day Preview
  1. **OVERALL: POSITIVE CATALYST IF ORCL CAN ADDRESS THE KEY DEBATES.** Tal expects Oracle’s analyst day to be a positive catalyst if management can provide greater clarity around the long-term growth framework and the capital required to deliver it. Despite strong earnings, continued OCI momentum and rapid RPO growth, ORCL shares are down 33% YTD and credit spreads have widened, with investor concerns centered on funding requirements, the potential timing mismatch between infrastructure investment and revenue realization, and uncertainty around future capex and potential equity financing. 
  2. **LONG-TERM TARGETS / RPO: ROOM TO RAISE THE REVENUE FRAMEWORK.** Tal believes Oracle **will raise its long-term revenue targets** , supported by RPO increasing from $455bn to $664bn since the last investor day. Current expectations have moved relatively little despite roughly $210bn of additional RPO: Street OCI revenue estimates of ~$131bn/$170bn for FY29/FY30 compare with Oracle’s prior targets of $129bn/$166bn, while Street total revenue of ~$183bn/$224bn remains around prior targets of $185bn/$225bn. Tal wants greater clarity on RPO conversion timing and composition, including exposure to OpenAI and growth from non-OpenAI customers, with an updated multi-year IaaS outlook potentially providing a clearer bridge between contracted demand and revenue.  
  3. **AI INFRASTRUCTURE ECONOMICS / EXECUTION: PRICING AND CAPACITY ARE KEY.** Tal believes improving AI infrastructure pricing should support stronger margins and faster payback periods, consistent with recent commentary from CoreWeave and Nebius. He wants greater disclosure around Oracle’s returns relative to the ~$10/watt economics discussed at the 2025 analyst day, particularly as power, equipment and construction costs rise. The $300bn OpenAI agreement is also in focus, including whether pricing is fixed or can adjust with capacity costs. At the same time, OCI growth remains dependent on bringing incremental active power online, making execution at major campuses, particularly New Mexico and Wisconsin, critical. Tal will look for updates on capacity ramp timelines, Project Jupiter’s ~1GW New Mexico site and any contingency plans following recent disruption headlines.  
  4. **CAPITAL STRUCTURE / FCF: HOW DOES ORACLE FUND THE BUILDOUT?** Financing is likely to be one of the most important debates at the analyst day given Oracle’s ~$169bn debt balance including leases and the scale of planned infrastructure investment. Tal wants management to clarify the expected mix of debt, equity and asset-backed financing, funding requirements over the next several years, and implications for capex and FCF. BofA models capex of ~$92bn in FY27 and ~$106bn in FY28, with FCF of -$33bn and -$38bn, respectively. Near term, Oracle’s 6.3% FY27 earnings yield is roughly in line with its after-tax bond yields, suggesting similar earnings dilution from debt versus equity issuance, although equity could alleviate financial-risk concerns while debt remains cheaper when using FY3 earnings yield as the closer proxy for cost of equity. A credible funding framework could therefore be important for both the equity and credit story.

** ****AMZN SETUP & EXPECTATIONS – Reports Thu. (10/29), after-market**

  * **OVERALL:** AMZN is up 8% YTD (vs. S&P up 12%). BofA is at Rev/EBIT of $202.0bn/$26.4bn vs. Street at $202.1bn/$26.1bn. Justin estimates 40% y/y AWS revenue growth (vs. Street at 38%).  Risk is higher growth and capacity demand could drive higher capex/lower FCF expectations in 2027.
  * **KEY METRIC – AWS Revs:** Justin sees upside potential for AWS driven by capacity growth, pricing increases, and strong traction for model use on the Bedrock platform.  Margins should benefit from increasing Trainium use and Bedrock expansion, though large AWS clients are trying to negotiate better capacity deals.
  * **KEY METRIC – 4Q revenue/profit guidance:**  AWS growth should be favorable vs Street sellside estimates.  Retail has conflicting data points around spend for Prime Big Deal Days in October, but elevated seasonal hiring (+20%) vs last year could suggest a solid holiday sales outlook.  Fuel costs in focus for margin outlook.
  * **POSITIONING INTO PRINT: Still one of the best performers and best sentiment in Internet sector, though concerns have grown on 2027 investment spend and need to raise capital (see debt issuance expectations chart below).   **AMZN’s 2027E P/E multiple has come down from 29.3x (2026 YE) to 23.4x today.  AMZN reports after META and GOOG, and timing could be favorable as AI investment expectations for the sector have been reset. Potential for Trainium 4 and LLM development catalysts at Re:Invent ahead.

    * Q4 GAAP EBIT Guide – **$33.1B**(Street $33.9B)
    * Q4 AWS Rev growth (reported) – **41.6%** (Street 39.4%)
    * 2026 GAAP EBIT – **$113B**(Street $110.2B)
    * 2027 GAAP EBIT – **$152B**(Street $141.6B)
    * 2026 Capex – **$225.5B**(Street $221.9B)
    * 2027 Capex – **$313B**(Street $285B)

    * Q3/Q4 CPU ASPs likely still strong (and solid GMs), Q4 units for Granite Rapids to improve a lot as well, which could contribute to better Q4 guide.
